query_text: A web page listing all the little shops and services in the neighborhood, where each place has a short description and a star rating that locals can leave, so you can quickly figure out which bakery or repair guy is actually worth visiting, and you can filter by category on the left side while the main area shows the listings with their community scores and a few recent comments right underneath.

A website where local artisans can show off what they make and sell, and regular people who bought from them can leave reviews and start little discussion threads about the products, so there is a left column for browsing by craft type and the main part shows each seller with their average rating and a link to their forum section where buyers compare notes and ask questions.

Create a web app that works like a community notice board where neighborhood shops and service people can post their promotions and special offers, so locals opening it in a browser can scroll through a feed of posts sorted by newest first, and each post has the business name, what they are offering, and a simple thumbs-up button so people can show which deals they think are worth sharing.

Make a website where neighbors can team up to buy things together from local independent shops, so you pick a deal that a shop has posted, see how many people have already joined, and once enough folks sign up the group order goes through, with a sidebar showing active deals organized by shop type and a progress bar on each one counting down to the minimum needed.

A browser-based app that collects all your loyalty stamp cards from different local stores into one place, so instead of carrying a stack of paper cards you just open this site, pick the shop, and tap to add a stamp when you buy something, and there is a section showing how close you are to a reward at each store all lined up so you can see your progress at a glance.

Make a web app that is a shared events calendar where local shop owners can each add their own events like sales, workshops, or tasting nights, so that anyone in the neighborhood can open it in a browser and see everything happening this month on a proper calendar view, and clicking on an event shows which business is hosting it along with whatever details they filled in.

Create a website that connects local service businesses so they can refer customers to each other, like a plumber pointing clients to a trusted electrician in the same network, with a directory page listing all the members by trade and each profile showing who they have referred and how many good reviews those referrals earned so you can trust the connections are real and not just random.

Build a web app where people can pre-order food from local vendors and schedule a curbside pickup time, so you open the site, browse what a vendor has available today, pick your items, and then choose a pickup window from a little time slot calendar, and the vendor side of the site shows all the incoming orders grouped by time slot so they know what to prepare and when.

Make a website where anyone in the neighborhood can post a small job they need help with, like moving a couch or fixing a leaky faucet, and people who want to help can respond with their availability and a rough price, with the board showing all open requests in the main area and a sidebar to filter by job type.

Need a browser-based site where a small community of people can pool their buying power and order together from tiny local vendors who cannot afford to sell one item at a time, so you log in, see what is currently open for group orders, add yourself to one, and pay when the order closes, with a section that shows each vendor and all their past fulfilled orders so you know they are reliable.

Need a web app where local shops can post flash sales that last only a few hours, with each deal showing a countdown timer ticking down to when it expires, so customers can open the site in a browser and see all active deals sorted by how soon they end, and shop owners use a simple form to post a new deal with the discount amount and end time.

Make a web platform where several small businesses in a neighborhood can collaborate on a shared newsletter, so each shop owner can log in and add their own section like a new product announcement or a special hours notice, and then someone reviews the combined draft in a preview pane before sending it out as one newsletter to everyone who has signed up to receive it.

Build a website where people can list gift cards from local shops that they are not going to use and swap or sell them to neighbors who actually want them, so the main page shows available cards grouped by store name with the remaining balance and asking price, and there is a simple way to message the person listing it to arrange the exchange without the whole thing getting overly complicated.

A job board website for the neighborhood where homeowners can post repair or handyman tasks they need done around the house, with each listing showing the type of job, a rough idea of the budget, and the area of town, and tradespeople can browse all the open jobs in a main feed while filtering by work type in a left-hand panel, and clicking a job shows the full details and a button to express interest.

Create a web app for small salons and barbershops that lets clients book appointments online without having to call or text back and forth, with a calendar showing which time slots are still open and which are taken, so the shop owner can block off days they are closed and clients just pick a date and time from a browser and receive a confirmation, saving everyone the hassle of missed calls and double bookings.

Create a simple website tool for freelance tradespeople like painters or electricians to generate invoices without messing around with spreadsheets every single time, where you type in the client name, the work done, the hours and rate, and it spits out a clean invoice you can download as a file, with a history page showing all the ones you have already sent so you are not scrambling to remember what you charged last month.

Create a web app where a small business owner can track what stock they have on hand without having to count everything by hand or dig through notebooks, so you enter your items and quantities, the app keeps track as you update them, and it automatically sends you an email when something drops below a number you set so you are not caught off guard when something runs out.

Create a web-based scheduling board for small restaurant teams where the owner sets up the week's shifts by dragging staff names into time slots, each team member can open the page in a browser to see when they are working, and there is a simple way to flag if someone cannot make a shift so the owner finds out right away.

A punch-card loyalty web app for neighborhood cafes that replaces those annoying little paper cards that always get lost, where a customer gives their phone number or email at the counter, the barista marks a visit on their account in the browser, and after ten visits the app automatically shows a free drink reward, so there is no printer needed and the cafe owner can see at a glance how many regulars they have.

Make a web tool for home repair businesses to quickly put together a price estimate without writing everything out from scratch, where you pick the type of work from a list, enter the square footage or number of items, and the tool calculates a total based on rates you set ahead of time, so you can show a client a proper quote right there in the browser.

Create a web app that tracks when business licenses are coming up for renewal and sends reminders before the deadline so you do not accidentally let one lapse, with a main page showing all your licenses listed by expiry date, the ones closest to expiring highlighted at the top, and a form for adding a new license by just typing in the name, the authority that issued it, and the renewal date.

A browser-based tool for sole proprietors that estimates how much tax they probably owe for the month without needing an accountant every single time, where you enter your income and your deductible expenses for the month and it shows a rough tax figure based on a rate you can adjust, with a running yearly total at the side so you are not blindsided by a huge bill when the year ends.

A menu builder web app for small food places where the owner can drag sections around and add items without any complicated setup, so instead of updating a blurry photo every time something changes you log into the site in a browser, build your menu by adding sections and items with prices, and get a shareable link customers can open to see what is available.

Create a web app for small business owners to manage their regular opening hours and easily override them for public holidays or one-off closures, because keeping that info updated in five different places is a nightmare, so the main screen shows the week's hours in a simple grid you can edit, and there is a separate section for adding exceptions like being closed on a specific holiday or having shorter hours for a special event.

A website for local retail shops that pulls in reviews from different review sites and shows them all together, so instead of jumping between tabs the shop owner just opens this web app and sees a feed of recent reviews sorted by date, with the source noted next to each one and a way to filter to just the negative ones so complaints do not get missed.
